newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet, with no slaughter steer or heifer sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Light bids early at $66.00 per cwt were passed by owners asking $68.00 to $69.00, they said.

Fed cattle prices this week were expected to be underpinned by outlooks for firm beef demand and smaller numbers of cattle on Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma showlists. Active sales last week at a top of $67.00 kept Panhandle feedlot marketings current, sources there said.
Sales in Kansas last week were not as active, which resulted in a modest number of cattle carried over to this week, cattle feeders there said.
But the carryover was not seen weighing on prices as many of the unsold cattle needed more days on feed, sources said.

Brisk beef sales last week inspired prospects for more of the same, which could fuel packer demand for fed cattle, some sources noted. Beef sales last week totaled 1,344 loads of fabricated cuts, according to USDA. However, the sales were achieved at lower prices, with the value of heavier-weight choice down $1.45 per cwt to end Friday at $102.70, USDA said.
The previous week's movement totaled 838 loads, and the price of heavier-weight choice beef rose $2.22, USDA said.
